arml-2006-team-01.prompt: A cylinder of height $10$ cm and radius $6$ cm is turning at $1$ revolution per minute. A paintbrush $4$ cm wide starts at the top as shown and slowly moves vertically down the cylinder at $1$ cm/minute. Compute the time in minutes it takes for the paintbrush to paint three-fifths of the lateral surface area of the cylinder.

arml-2006-team-02.prompt: Let $[x]$ be the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$. Compute all values of $x$ so that the product $\left[x-\tfrac12\right]\left[x+\tfrac12\right]$ is prime.

arml-2006-team-03.prompt: In $\triangle CBA$, $\overline{CD}$ and $\overline{AE}$ are medians (with $D$ on $\overline{AB}$ and $E$ on $\overline{CB}$), $\overline{FC}\parallel\overline{AB}$, and $F,E,H$ are collinear (with $H$ on $\overline{AB}$), $C,G,D$ are collinear and $A,G,E$ are collinear, as shown. The area of $FCGE$ is $7$ and the area of $EGDH$ is $11$. Compute the area of $\triangle CBA$.

arml-2006-team-04.prompt: For $x$ in radians, if $\tan x=\dfrac ab$, $\tan2x=\dfrac b{a+b}$, and the least positive value for $x$ equals $\tan^{-1}k$, compute $k$.

arml-2006-team-05.prompt: Let $N$ be an integer such that $1\le N\le2006^2$. Compute the number of values of $N$ such that there exists a factor of $N$, call it $a$, such that $\left|\sqrt N-a\right|\le1$.

arml-2006-team-06.prompt: There are $N$ positive integers $b$ such that $10\le\log_{10}\left(\log_{10}b\right)\le100$. Let $S$ be the sum of the digits of $N$. Compute the sum of the digits of $S$.

arml-2006-team-07.prompt:
Shown are rows $1$, $2$, and $3$ of Pascal's triangle (row $n$ has the entries $\binom ni$, $0\le i\le n$; row $1$ is $1\ 1$, row $2$ is $1\ 2\ 1$, row $3$ is $1\ 3\ 3\ 1$). Let $\{a_i\}$, $\{b_i\}$ and $\{c_i\}$ be the sequence, from left to right, of elements in the $2005^{\text{th}}$, $2006^{\text{th}}$ and $2007^{\text{th}}$ rows, respectively, with the leftmost element occurring at $i=0$. Compute
$$\sum_{i=0}^{2006}\frac{b_i}{c_i}-\sum_{i=0}^{2005}\frac{a_i}{b_i}.$$

arml-2006-team-08.prompt: An empty down elevator opens its doors on the $6^{\text{th}}$ floor. It will stop at every floor unless it gets stuck. At each of the floors $6$ through $2$, if there is no one in the elevator, the people waiting flip a coin. If it is heads, one person gets on; if it is tails, no one gets on. At each of the floors $5$ through $2$, if there are $1$ or $2$ people in the elevator, the people waiting flip a coin. If it is heads, one person gets on and no one gets off; if it is tails, one person on the elevator gets off and no one gets on. If there are three people in the elevator at any time, it gets stuck. Compute the probability that the elevator gets stuck before reaching the first floor.

arml-2006-team-09.prompt: Compute the number of ordered triples $(a,b,c)$ of integers with $b,c\ge0$ such that $5!\cdot a^b-4!\cdot a^c=3456$.

arml-2006-team-10.prompt: Let $n$ be a six-digit positive integer that is not a palindrome but which becomes a six-digit palindrome if two of its digits are interchanged. Compute the number of $n$. Note: a six-digit integer does not start with $0$.
